mike: Hey folks — canary allocator change (PR #4128) landed and we see OOMs in long chat sessions on dedicated nodes. Repro: ./bench/run_chat.sh --model redwood-3b --seq 2048 --concurrency 4

Logs:
```
[2025-11-12T09:12:03Z] OOM: alloc failed 104857600
[2025-11-12T09:12:03Z] process memory: rss=6.2G, vm=18G
```

I tried toggling jemalloc config (MALLOC_CONF="oversize_threshold:3") and fragmentation seems worse. Can someone help with heap profiling and fragmentation metrics? I left a canary image: gcr.io/redwood/runtime:canary-20251112

I'm attaching the reproducer script: ./scripts/repro_long_chat.sh

Any quick checklists I should run?

aj: :eyes: Thanks Mike. Two quick asks: (1) capture a heap profile (tcmalloc/pprof or gperftools) and (2) run with MALLOC_CONF="background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:1000" and compare. If using jemalloc, enable stats_print and use mallctl to dump stats. Also please paste output of /proc/<pid>/smaps and the mallctl stats (arena, active, dirty).

Run these to record heap (tcmalloc):
```
LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/libtcmalloc.so HEAPPROFILE=./heap ./bench/run_chat.sh --model redwood-3b --seq 2048 --concurrency 4
pprof --text ./bin/runtime ./heap.heap > heap.txt
```
For jemalloc use:
```
MALLOC_CONF=stats_print:true ./bench/run_chat.sh --model ...
# then check logs for jemalloc stats or call mallctl("stats.print") programmatically
```
I'll allocate time to look after lunch.

sara: I can repro on one dedicated node. I'll capture smaps and run `smem -k` and check cgroups. Also will run with --enable-kv-cache=false to see if KV cache is inflating.

danielle: From model side, long seqs + continuous KV caching cause big KV growth. Suggest enabling prefix eviction after 512 tokens and measure. Also try int8 quantized linear ops for the transformer layers — should reduce RSS.

ci-bot: perfbench job 7123 queued for gcr.io/redwood/runtime:canary-20251112 - will post artifacts to https://artifacts.redwood.internal/7123 when finished

mike: Thanks — attached partial heap dump (artifacts link above) and mallctl stats snippet:
```
allocated: 7340032000
active: 8534944000
mapped: 10737418240
metadata: 34567840
```
Looks like active >> allocated. Could be fragmentation / arena retention.

aj: active > allocated suggests fragmentation/arena retention. Try enabling background_thread:true and lowering decay (dirty_decay_ms/merge_threshold) so pages return to OS sooner. If still high, run `mallctl("arena.<n>.purge")` to force release and check RSS delta. Also run jeprof/pprof to see which allocation sites dominate by size (not just count).

sara: I've run the perf job; artifacts available: https://artifacts.redwood.internal/7123/heap/ (heap profiles + smaps). Early result: RSS drops ~600MB after mallctl purge, but grows back under ~10m of traffic.

mike: I'll instrument allocator stats in the runtime and add a /debug/alloc endpoint that dumps jemalloc stats and top allocation sites. Pushing a patch to canary now (will tag the image when complete).

aj: Great. Let's reconvene async — post results here. If we find a reliable mitigation (config tweak or small allocator shim), we'll push a short-lived override for Dedicated nodes. I'll open a follow-up PR to adjust MALLOC_CONF defaults once we have reproducible numbers.

sara: FYI I also saw higher fragmentation on hosts with many short-lived connections (HTTP keepalive churn). Might be worth cross-checking connection patterns vs RSS.

mike: noted — I'll add connection churn metrics to the perfbench run. Thanks all :pray:
